title: Introduce windowed traffic-shift detector and successive-degradation rollout guard
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Add traffic-shift-aware canary detector to suppress false positives during staged rollouts; add successive-degradation guard to detect progressive regressions across multiple windows; new config knobs for window duration and required consecutive failures.
body: Context and motivation: Recent canary incidents (tracked ENG-3421) showed that upward shifts in request mix during staged traffic ramps and transient downstream slowdowns produced false-positive canary alerts and caused unnecessary rollbacks. This PR adds two related protections: a windowed traffic-shift detector that detects and discounts significant traffic-shape changes during evaluation windows, and a successive-degradation rollout guard that requires regressions to persist across multiple consecutive windows before triggering automatic rollback. Summary of changes: 1) New detector module perf_canary/detectors/traffic_shift_detector.py implementing a sliding-window KL-divergence and chi-squared test on binned request signatures; 2) New guard perf_canary/guards/successive_degradation_guard.py that maintains a short-lived state machine across N windows and only escalates when threshold-crossing occurs K times in a row; 3) Canary config schema extended (canary_schema.yaml) with traffic_shift_window_ms, traffic_shift_threshold, consecutive_failure_count; 4) Instrumentation and tagging updates to emit traffic-shape fingerprints (request_path_buckets, model_size_bucket, token_length_bucket) alongside existing latency/throughput metrics; 5) Integration of guard into canary-runner pipeline: detectors are evaluated after metric aggregation but before final verdict; 6) Unit and integration tests added plus a new e2e scenario simulating staged rollouts with synthetic traffic shifts; 7) Dashboard and alert playbook additions (grafana/dashboards/canary-traffic-shift.json, docs/playbooks/traffic-shift.md). Commits (high-level): - Implement traffic shift detector and unit tests - Add successive-degradation guard and state persistence util - Extend canary config and validation - Hook detectors into canary-runner decision path - Add e2e scenario and flaky-run mitigation - Docs and dashboards update - Address review comments and threshold tuning Changed areas (high level): - perf_canary/detectors/traffic_shift_detector.py (new) - perf_canary/guards/successive_degradation_guard.py (new) - perf_canary/canary_runner.py (modified) - perf_canary/schema/canary_schema.yaml (modified) - tests/unit/test_traffic_shift.py (new) - tests/integration/test_successive_degradation.py (new) - grafana/dashboards/canary-traffic-shift.json (new) - docs/playbooks/traffic-shift.md (new) Tests and CI: Initial CI run: lint/static-analysis passed, unit tests passed, integration tests passed, e2e suite failed (timing-sensitive scenario) with two flaky assertions related to sampler timing. After adding a short jitter and increasing the synthetic load ramp tolerance the e2e suite passed on a rerun. Patch notes in CI: mark two e2e cases as flaky and added a follow-up linear ticket ENG-3490 to harden the harness. Review conversation (summary): - Anika: Asked for rationale behind KL vs simple percentile-based divergence; requested a justification in comments and an example showing noisy upstream vs real traffic-shift. - Author (Maya): Added bench script results in tests and inline docstring explaining why KL plus chi-squared gating reduces sensitivity to tail noise. - Liam: Questioned state persistence window for successive_degradation_guard and suggested bounded memory model; requested max-state TTL. - Author: Implemented TTL of 5 minutes and added a bounded deque with explicit eviction to prevent unbounded memory. - Ravi: Requested explicit rollout annotation when detector suppresses an alert (so ops knows why automatic rollback was skipped). - Author: Added an annotation path and updated the playbook. Approvals and merge: After two rounds of minor changes and one follow-up commit to stabilize e2e timing, Anika and Liam approved. CI green on final run. Merged via squash on 2026-02-22. Backwards compatibility and config: Default behavior is opt-in via canary config flags; detectors are disabled unless traffic_shift_window_ms > 0. This makes the change non-breaking. Follow-ups: ENG-3490 (harden e2e harness), ENG-3515 (tune defaults after 2 weeks of canary telemetry). Operational notes: - New metrics emitted: canary.traffic_shape.kld, canary.traffic_shape.pvalue, canary.guard.successive_degradation.count - Dashboards include a 5/15/60s breakdown and an example playbook for noisy downstreams. - Rollout gating semantics: the guard only triggers an automated rollback when consecutive_failure_count >= configured value; otherwise the canary is marked for manual review. Implementation details for reviewers: - Traffic fingerprinting uses 8 coarse buckets by path, 4 by model size, 6 by token length; these were chosen to balance cardinality vs signal. - Detector computes KL over fingerprints with an adaptive floor to avoid divide-by-zero on rare buckets; chi-squared test is used as a secondary gate for small sample sizes. - Successive-degradation guard persists minimal state keyed by canary_run_id in the ephemeral store used by canary-runner (same store as existing short-lived counters). - Unit tests include parameterized scenarios that simulate noisy tails and true traffic-shifts. - Integration tests include an A/B style rollback simulation. Rollout: This was first enabled for internal perf-canary experiments, then enabled for a subset of customer-facing rollouts behind a feature flag. Observability and alerting: Added annotations and an alert rule that fires an informational alert when a traffic-shift is detected but suppressed (so SRE can triage).
